i < numNodes * numNodes; ++i) {\n        dist[i] = rangeMin + (unsigned int)(range * rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX);\n    }\n    \n    // Set diagonal to zero (distance from node to itself is 0)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n        dist[idx2(i, i, numNodes)] = 0;\n    }\n}\n\nvoid initializePathMatrix(std::vector<unsigned int>& path, const size_t numNodes) {\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < numNodes; ++j) {\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n            path[idx2(i, j, numNodes)] = j;\n            path[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = i;\n        }\n        path[idx2(j, j, numNodes)] = j;\n    }\n}\n\nvoid floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, \n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path, \n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Classic Floyd-Warshall algorithm\n    // For each intermediate node k\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < numNodes; ++k) {\n        // For each source node i\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n            // For each destination node j\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < numNodes; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int distIJ = dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distIK = dist[idx2(k, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distKJ = dist[idx2(j, k, numNodes)];\n                \n                const unsigned int newDist = distIK + distKJ;\n                \n                if (newDist < distIJ) {\n                    dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = newDist;\n                    path[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = k;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Basic sanity checks\n    \n    // 1. Diagonal should be zero\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n        if (dist[idx2(i, i, numNodes)] != 0) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: diagonal element [%zu,%zu] is not zero\\n\", i, i);\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // 2. {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < std::min(numNodes, static_cast<size_t>(10)); ++j) {\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < numNodes; ++k) {\n                const unsigned int distIJ = dist[idx2(j, i, Check for overflow before addition\n                if (distIK < INF && distKJ < INF) {\n                    if (distIK + distKJ < distIJ) {\n                        printf(\"Validation failed: triangle inequality violated at [%zu,%zu,%zu]\\n\", \n                               i, j, k);\n                        return false;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of \n    printf(\"Floyd-Warshall All-Pairs Shortest Path Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Number of nodes: %zu\\n\", numNodes);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    // Allocate matrices\n    std::vector<unsigned int> dist(numNodes * numNodes);\n    std::vector<unsigned int> path(numNodes * numNodes);\n    \n    // Initialize\n    printf(\"Initializing My main concern is the constexpr index function being called from device code — I should mark it __host__ __device__ so it works properly, or just inline the index formula directly in the kernel to avoid the issue entirely.\n\nNow I'm sketching the Floyd-Warshall kernel: each thread handles one (i,j) pair, reading dist[i][k] and dist[k][j], and updating dist[i][j] and the path matrix if a shorter route through k is found. I'm wary of a race condition — within a single k-iteration, some threads could read dist[i][k] or dist[k][j] while other threads are simultaneously writing to those same cells.\n\nI reasoned through this hazard: since dist[k][k] is always 0 and never goes negative, the only possible writes to row/column k would require an improvement over 0+0=0, which can't happen, so those cells stay stable throughout the iteration — no race condition. With unsigned distances and no INF sentinel in play, overflow isn't a concern either, matching the original logic.\n\nLaunching 512 kernels (one per k) with n² threads each should work, though I'm considering whether tiling multiple k values per kernel using shared memory could improve performance further.\n\nFor the implementation, I'm planning to have floydWarshall handle cudaMalloc, host-to-device copy, the iteration loop, device-to-host copy, and cleanup internally, with timing in main wrapping that whole call — and I'll call cudaFree(0) beforehand as a warm-up so CUDA context initialization doesn't pollute the measured time.\n\nI should also check the cmake and nvcc versions first, then build a reference CPU version separately with g++ into a temp directory for output comparison before writing the GPU code. A quick todo list would help organize these steps.\n\n","time":{"start":1793061791385,"end":1793061823392},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793061838072,"sessionID":"ses_e85307174ffeZlmN674JqxGl2C","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"edit","callID":"toolu_01EWxSsGhYbZsAprkWAUDFfB","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/floydwarshall_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r4/floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp","oldString":"void floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, \n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path, \n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Classic Floyd-Warshall algorithm\n    // For each intermediate node k\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < numNodes; ++k) {\n        // For each source node i\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n            // For each destination node j\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < numNodes; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int distIJ = dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distIK = dist[idx2(k, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distKJ = dist[idx2(j, k, numNodes)];\n                \n                const unsigned int newDist = distIK + distKJ;\n                \n                if (newDist < distIJ) {\n                    dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = newDist;\n                    path[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = k;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}","newString":"// One Floyd-Warshall relaxation step for intermediate node k, applied to every\n// (i, j) pair in parallel. Row k and column k are never modified during step k\n// (dist[k][k] == 0 and all weights are non-negative), so every thread reads\n// stable values and each (i, j) is written by exactly one thread. The result is\n// therefore identical to the sequential k-i-j loop nest.\n__global__ void floydWarshallStep(unsigned int* __restrict__ dist,\n                                  unsigned int* __restrict__ path,\n                                  const size_t numNodes,\n                                  const size_t k) {\n    const size_t j = blockIdx.x * static_cast<size_t>(blockDim.x) + threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t i = blockIdx.y * static_cast<size_t>(blockDim.y) + threadIdx.y;\n    if (i >= numNodes || j >= numNodes) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    const unsigned int distIJ = dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)];\n    const unsigned int distIK = dist[idx2(k, i, numNodes)];\n    const unsigned int distKJ = dist[idx2(j, k, numNodes)];\n\n    const unsigned int newDist = distIK + distKJ;\n\n    if (newDist < distIJ) {\n        dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = newDist;\n        path[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = static_cast<unsigned int>(k);\n    }\n}\n\nvoid floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, \n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path, \n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    if (numNodes == 0) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    const size_t count = numNodes * numNodes;\n    unsigned int* dDist = nullptr;\n    unsigned int* dPath = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dDist, count * sizeof(unsigned int)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dPath, count * sizeof(unsigned int)));\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dDist, dist.data(), count * sizeof(unsigned int), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dPath, path.data(), count * sizeof(unsigned int), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n    // 2D launch: x spans destination nodes j, y spans source nodes i\n    constexpr unsigned int BLOCK_X = 32;\n    constexpr unsigned int BLOCK_Y = 8;\n    const dim3 block(BLOCK_X, BLOCK_Y);\n    const dim3 grid(static_cast<unsigned int>((numNodes + BLOCK_X - 1) / BLOCK_X),\n                    static_cast<unsigned int>((numNodes + BLOCK_Y - 1) / BLOCK_Y));\n\n    // Intermediate node k must be processed sequentially; each step is fully parallel\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < numNodes; ++k) {\n        floydWarshallStep<<<grid, block>>>(dDist, dPath, numNodes, k);\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dist.data(), dDist, count * sizeof(unsigned int), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(path.data(), dPath, count * sizeof(unsigned int), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dDist));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dPath));\n}"},"output":"Edit applied successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"diff":"Index: /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/floydwarshall_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r4/floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp\n===================================================================\n--- /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/floydwarshall_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r4/floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp\n+++ /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/floydwarshall_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r4/floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp\n@@ -52,31 +52,69 @@\n         path[idx2(j, j, numNodes)] = j;\n     }\n }\n \n+// One Floyd-Warshall relaxation step for intermediate node k, applied to every\n+// (i, j) pair in parallel. {"type":"text","timestamp":1793061897585,"sessionID":"ses_e85307174ffeZlmN674JqxGl2C","part":{"id":"prt_17ad13800001MGPr3RC4NkRT3V","messageID":"msg_17ad1342a001vQ78lxZIxi08CN","sessionID":"ses_e85307174ffeZlmN674JqxGl2C","type":"text","text":"The Floyd-Warshall benchmark now runs on the GPU unconditionally. The executable name is unchanged, and the only files touched are `floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp` and `floydwarshall/CMakeLists.txt`.\n\n**Approach**\n- The `.cpp` file is compiled as CUDA via `set_source_files_properties(... LANGUAGE CUDA)`, so no new source file was needed.\n- Each intermediate node `k` launches one kernel over all (i, j) pairs in a 32×8 thread block grid. Launches on the same stream run in order, so the k-sequencing is preserved.\n- Row k and column k never change during step k, because `dist[k][k] == 0` and weights are non-negative. That means every thread reads stable values and each (i, j) is written by one thread only. The result, including the `path` matrix, matches the sequential loop exactly.\n- Matrices are copied to the device once, all k-steps run on the device, and results are copied back once.\n\n**Verification**\n- Output (min/max/samples/hash) is identical to the original CPU build for n = 512, 1000, and 33, with `-v -r` validation passing.\n\n**Timing** (RTX 3090, measured on the same machine)\n\n| n | Original CPU | CUDA version |\n|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 165 ms | 24 ms |\n| 2048 | 9384 ms | 88 ms |\n| 4096 | — | 503 ms |\n\nThe timed region includes host-device transfers but excludes CUDA context creation, which runs before the timer starts.\n\n**Notes**\n- The build uses `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native` (requires CMake 3.24+ when the variable is not set by the user; the minimum is still declared as 3.18, so older CMake versions need to set the architecture explicitly). Pass `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86` if the native detection is not available.\n- Further speedup would likely require a blocked/tiled Floyd-Warshall. That would change the order in which intermediate values are seen, which could alter the `path` matrix. The `path` matrix is not printed or validated, but I kept the exact per-k ordering to preserve the original semantics.\n- The unused `output.txt` and the build directory were left out of the project; the build was done in `/run/llm-eval/state/tmp/opencode/build`.","time":{"start":1793061894144,"end":1793061897581}}}
